change_manifest.purpose: Shared helper: queue_skill <skill> <reason> <context-json> with atomic write and dedup key
UserPromptSubmit drain: surface queue entries as additionalContext with TTL and 3-entry cap
UserPromptSubmit pre-drain: regex-match correction keywords, queue correction-capture
PostToolUse Edit|Write on docs/specs/*.md: detect status: approved transition, queue planning-and-task-breakdown
Five adversarial scenarios covering false-positive corrections, pollution, dedup, kill-switch, TTL
SC1 integration test — correction keyword triggers queue write and drain emission
SC2 integration test — spec status: approved transition queues planning-and-task-breakdown
SC3 integration test — MTK_HOOKS_TIER2=0 silences all tier-2 behavior
SC4 integration test — 24h-old queue entries are skipped and counted as expired
Wire UserPromptSubmit (correction-trigger + drain) and extend PostToolUse Edit|Write with spec-approval-trigger; add MTK_HOOKS_TIER2 env
Add S3.13 tier classification, S3.14 queue protocol, S3.15 kill-switch requirement
Register new files; bump version to 6.4.0; update updated date
Bump version to 6.4.0 to sync with manifest per C0.1
Add .claude/queue/ so queue entries are never committed
Add one-line row documenting MTK_HOOKS_TIER2 kill-switch in Skill Routing section
Validate new manifest entries exist, new S3.13-15 rule IDs present, skill-queue.sh is executable

public_contracts.signature: hook event PostToolUse[Edit|Write] -> hooks/spec-approval-trigger.sh (additive alongside existing scope-guard)
analytics schema: .claude/analytics.json adds fields queue_writes, queue_drains, queue_expired (integer)

success_criteria.description: With MTK_HOOKS_TIER2=1, correction keyword in user prompt queues correction-capture and the next turn's additionalContext lists it
With MTK_HOOKS_TIER2=1, writing a spec with status: approved queues planning-and-task-breakdown with the spec path
With MTK_HOOKS_TIER2=0, no triggers write to the queue and the drain is silent
Queue entries older than 24 hours are skipped by the drain and counted as expired in analytics
.claude/analytics.json gains queue_writes, queue_drains, queue_expired counters that increment correctly
success_criteria.verification: diff analytics.json before and after a hook run

success_criteria.description: All five pressure scenarios (casual no, long session, repeat-save dedup, kill-switch, TTL) pass when run against a live session
bash scripts/validate-toolkit.sh passes after all batches — manifest entries exist, frontmatter valid, versions synced

out_of_scope: Phase 2: additional triggers — SessionEnd->handoff, test-failure nudge, commit->spec-drift-detection
Phase 3: headless parallel reviewer fanout via claude -p sub-agents on gh pr create
Cross-repo analytics aggregation (nightly GitHub Action, separate from the plugin)
Team-shared queue across machines — queue stays per-workspace
assumptions: Claude Code UserPromptSubmit hook produces {"additionalContext": "..."} on stdout (confirmed in Batch 1; fallback to {"context": ...} shape if not)
PostToolUse Edit|Write hooks receive stdin JSON with tool_input.file_path — already used by scope-guard.sh
${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} and relative hooks/ paths both resolve correctly in settings.json hook commands
Engineer consents to small prompt excerpt (<=500 chars) in gitignored local queue files for <=24h
Spec approval is expressed via '- **Status:** approved' or YAML frontmatter status: approved — a convention spec-driven-development will adopt going forward
risks: R1 False-positive correction detection on casual 'no' in long sentences — mitigated by tight regex and pressure scenario 1
R2 Context pollution from unbounded drain emission — mitigated by 3-entry cap, duplicate collapse, 24h TTL
R3 Race between concurrent hook fires writing queue entries — mitigated by atomic temp-file-then-rename with hash-suffixed filenames
R4 Agent ignores drain reminder — accepted; tier-2 is propose-not-act; toolkit-health surfaces the drain-but-not-invoked ratio
R5 Spec approval detection is convention-based and may miss non-conforming markers — documented convention, revisited if misses are frequent
R6 Pre-existing version drift (manifest 6.3.2 vs plugin 6.3.1, C0.1 violation) — resolved incidentally by bumping both to 6.4.0 in Batch 4
